nodes.summary: The closed walk with vertex list $[2, 8]$ has edge list $[(2, 8), (8, 2)]$, and the closed walk with vertex list $[9]$ (a loop at $9$) has edge list $[(9, 9)]$.
nodes.title: Edges of the closed walks $2 \to 8 \to 2$ and $9 \to 9$

nodes.summary: For a list $[v_0, \dots, v_{r-1}]$ of natural numbers, read as the vertex list of a closed walk, the edge list is $[(v_0, v_1), \dots, (v_{r-2}, v_{r-1}), (v_{r-1}, v_0)]$: each vertex is paired with the next one, and the last vertex with the first. A single vertex $[v_0]$ gives the loop $[(v_0, v_0)]$, and the empty list gives the empty edge list.
nodes.title: Edge list of a closed walk

nodes.summary: For a multiset $I$ of lists of natural numbers, each read as the vertex list of a closed walk, write $C_j$ for the edge list of $j \in I$. The multiset union $C_I = \biguplus_{j \in I} C_j$ is the multiset of all these edges, counted with multiplicity: each list $j$ contributes its edges as often as $j$ occurs in $I$.
nodes.title: Multiset union of cycle edges

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers. If $(d_1, d_2)$ is an edge of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, then there are natural numbers $c_1$ and $c_2$ with $c_1 \le n - 1$ and $c_2 \le n - 1$ such that $b c_2 - c_1 = n d_2 - d_1$ as integers.
nodes.title: Every mother-graph edge induces a carry transition

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $b$ and $d_0, \dots, d_k$ be natural numbers and let $\sigma$ be a permutation of $\{0, \dots, k\}$ such that $(d_k, \dots, d_0)_b$ is an $(n, b, \sigma)$-permutiple. Then there is a permutation $\hat\sigma$ of $\{0, \dots, k\}$ such that $(d_k, \dots, d_0)_b$ is also an $(n, b, \hat\sigma)$-permutiple and the digits along each cycle of $\hat\sigma$ are distinct: for all $j \in \{0, \dots, k\}$ and all…
nodes.title: Every permutiple has a cycle-preserving digit permutation

nodes.summary: Let $1 < n < b$ and let $I$ be a multiset of cycles of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, with multiset union of cycle edges $C_I$ and multi-image union $\Delta_I$. Then $\Delta_I$ is $L$-Eulerian if and only if there is an $(n, b)$-permutiple string $s$ whose multiset of entries is $C_I$.
nodes.title: $L$-Eulerian criterion for permutiple strings

nodes.summary: Let $1 < n < b$ and let $I$ be a multiset of cycles of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, with multiset union of cycle edges $C_I$ and multi-image union $\Delta_I$. If $\Delta_I$ has an Eulerian circuit beginning and ending at the zero state, then there is an $(n, b)$-permutiple string $s$ whose multiset of entries is $C_I$.
nodes.title: Eulerian circuits through zero yield permutiple strings

nodes.summary: Read a multiset $D$ of pairs of natural numbers as the multi-edges $(c_1, c_2)$ of a directed multigraph. Then $D$ has an Eulerian circuit beginning and ending with the zero state when there is a nonempty list of pairs whose multiset of entries is $D$ (so it uses every multi-edge exactly once), in which each multi-edge ends where the next one begins, the first one starts at $0$ and the last one ends at $0$.
nodes.title: Eulerian circuit through the zero state

nodes.summary: On the input string $(d_0, \hat d_0)(d_1, \hat d_1)(d_2, \hat d_2)(d_3, \hat d_3) = (0,0)(2,3)(1,2)(3,1)$, the carries $c_0, c_1, c_2, c_3, c_4$ of the $(2, 4)$-Hoey–Sloane machine are $0, 0, 1, 1, 0$.
nodes.title: Carries of the $(2, 4)$-Hoey–Sloane machine on $(0,0)(2,3)(1,2)(3,1)$

nodes.title: Carries of the Hoey–Sloane machine

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $b$, the language $L$ of the $(n, b)$-Hoey–Sloane machine is the set of strings $s$ of pairs of natural numbers such that the machine, reading $s$ from left to right, can go from state $0$ to state $0$. In particular the empty string belongs to $L$.
nodes.title: Language of the Hoey–Sloane machine

nodes.summary: In the $(4, 10)$-Hoey–Sloane multigraph the label $(2, 8)$ sits on the multi-edge from state $0$ to state $3$, and the label $(1, 7)$ sits on the loop at state $3$: the Hoey–Sloane transition sends $(2, 8)$ to $(0, 3)$ and $(1, 7)$ to $(3, 3)$.
nodes.title: Two multi-edges of the $(4, 10)$-Hoey–Sloane multigraph

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$ and $b$ and a pair $e = (d_1, d_2)$ of natural numbers, the multi-edge of the $(n, b)$-Hoey–Sloane multigraph carrying the label $e$ is $(c_1, c_2)$, where $c_1 = \lambda(d_1 + (b - n) d_2)$ with $\lambda$ the least non-negative residue modulo $b$ (computed in the integers), and $c_2 = \lfloor (n d_2 - d_1 + c_1) / b \rfloor$, replaced by $0$ when negative. nodes.title: Hoey–Sloane transition of a digit pair

Let $E = \{(d_j, \hat d_j) : 0 \le j \le k\}$ be the set of inputs of $s$. Then every $e \in E$ lies on a directed cycle with edges in $E$:…

The $(n, b)$-Hoey-Sloane machine can go from state $c$ to state $c'$ reading $s$ from left to right when there are natural numbers $c_0, c_1, \dots, c_m$ with $c_0 = c$ and $c_m = c'$ such that, for each $1 \le i \le m$, the input $e_i$ moves state $c_{i-1}$ to state $c_i$ in…
nodes.title: Runs of the Hoey-Sloane machine

nodes.summary: Let $1 < n < b$, let $e = (d_1, d_2)$ be an edge of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, and let $(c_1, c_2)$ be the Hoey-Sloane transition of $e$, that is, $c_1 = \lambda(d_1 + (b - n) d_2)$ and $c_2 = (n d_2 - d_1 + c_1) / b$, where $\lambda$ is the least non-negative residue modulo $b$. Then the input $e$ moves state $c_1$ to state $c_2$ in one transition of the $(n, b)$-Hoey-Sloane machine.
nodes.title: Hoey-Sloane transitions are transitions of the machine

nodes.summary: Let $n \le b$. If an input $e$ moves state $c_1$ to state $c_2$ and also moves state $\hat c_1$ to state $\hat c_2$, each in one transition of the $(n, b)$-Hoey-Sloane machine, then $c_1 = \hat c_1$ and $c_2 = \hat c_2$.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of Hoey-Sloane transitions

nodes.summary: Let $n$, $b$, $c_1$, $c_2$, $d_1$ and $d_2$ be natural numbers. The input $e = (d_1, d_2)$ moves state $c_1$ to state $c_2$ in one transition of the $(n, b)$-Hoey-Sloane machine $\Gamma$ when $c_1 < n$, $c_2 < n$, $(d_1, d_2)$ is an edge of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, and $b c_2 - c_1 = n d_2 - d_1$ in the integers (Equation (1)).
nodes.title: Transitions of the Hoey-Sloane machine

nodes.summary: The input string $(d_0, \hat d_0) \cdots (d_3, \hat d_3) = (0,0)(2,3)(1,2)(3,1)$ belongs to the language $L$ of the $(2, 4)$-Hoey–Sloane machine.
nodes.title: The string $(0,0)(2,3)(1,2)(3,1)$ lies in the $(2, 4)$-Hoey–Sloane language

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers. An input string $(d_0, \hat d_0) \cdots (d_k, \hat d_k)$ of pairs of natural numbers belongs to the language $L$ of the $(n, b)$-Hoey–Sloane machine when, with $c_0, \dots, c_{k+1}$ the carries of the machine on this string, every input $(d_j, \hat d_j)$ is an edge of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, $b$ divides $n \hat d_j - d_j + c_j$ for every $0 \le j \le k$, and $c_{k+1} = 0$.
nodes.title: Hoey–Sloane words

The multigraph $D$ is $L$-Eulerian when $0$ is a vertex of $D$, every vertex $u$ of $D$ reaches every vertex $v$ of $D$ along a (possibly empty) directed path of multi-edges in $D$, and for every natural number $c$ the number of multi-edges in $D$ ending…
nodes.title: $L$-Eulerian multigraphs

nodes.summary: Let $n$ and $b$ be natural numbers. A list $[v_0, \dots, v_{r-1}]$ of natural numbers is a (directed) cycle of the $(n, b)$-mother graph when it is nonempty, has no repeated entry, and each of its edges $(v_0, v_1), \dots, (v_{r-2}, v_{r-1}), (v_{r-1}, v_0)$ is an edge of the $(n, b)$-mother graph. In particular a one-element list $[v]$ is a cycle when $(v, v)$ is an edge of the mother graph.
nodes.title: Cycles of the mother graph

nodes.summary: In the $(4, 10)$-mother graph, $(2, 8)$ and $(9, 9)$ are edges and $(2, 1)$ is not. With $\lambda$ the least non-negative residue modulo ten, $\lambda(2 + 6 \cdot 8) = 0 \le 3$ and $\lambda(9 + 6 \cdot 9) = 3 \le 3$, while $\lambda(2 + 6 \cdot 1) = 8 > 3$.
nodes.title: Sample edges of the $(4, 10)$-mother graph

nodes.summary: In the $(2, 4)$-mother graph, the pair $(0, 2)$ is an edge, since $\lambda(0 + (4 - 2) \cdot 2) = \lambda(4) = 0 \le 1$, and the pair $(0, 1)$ is not an edge, since $\lambda(0 + (4 - 2) \cdot 1) = \lambda(2) = 2 > 1$, where $\lambda$ is the least non-negative residue modulo $4$.
nodes.title: An edge and a non-edge of the $(2, 4)$-mother graph

nodes.summary: Let $1 < n < b$ and let $s$ be an $(n, b)$-permutiple string. Then every input $(d, \hat d)$ of $s$ is an edge of the $(n, b)$-mother graph, and $\hat d$ reaches $d$ along a (possibly empty) directed path in the graph whose edges are the inputs of $s$, so $(d, \hat d)$ lies on a directed cycle of that graph. In this sense the inputs of $s$ form a union of cycles of the mother graph.
nodes.title: Inputs of a permutiple string lie on mother-graph cycles

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
